text: ATM Audience Dashboard · written Oct 12, 2026 · daily figures through Oct 4 · monthly figures Sep 1–28
Conversation is up, reach is down, and partners and collabs did the lifting.

LinkedIn drew far more comments in September while impressions fell a quarter from August. The posts that travelled were the ones a guest, honoree or partner shared: reposts with their own words took a post to 7–8 times its organic engagement, and Instagram's best posts were all collabs. Instagram reach is fading into October, YouTube is now all organic and adding subscribers faster than the ad flight did, and the newsletter list grew on imports while clicks per delivered email fell.

Sources: LinkedIn page analytics and admin, Meta Business Suite and Instagram Insights, YouTube Analytics and Studio, GA4, Search Console, beehiiv, monday.com. Daily figures refresh each time the page opens; monthly figures are from the Sep 29 pull; the baseline audit at the end is from September.
The read · Sep 1 to Oct 4, 2026
What the numbers say, and what to do about it
One reading of every source on this page. Each point cites the section that holds the evidence.

title: LinkedIn: fewer impressions, more conversation.
text: Organic impressions were 54,039 in September, down 25% on August, and reach per post sits 25% below the June–August benchmark (901 against 1,196). Comments went the other way: 161 on posts published in the 30 days to Oct 5, against 60 in the 30 days before. LinkedIn's own engagement rate held near 8.7%. (Now; A)

title: Partners carried the reach where they took part.
text: Reposts with the partner's own words took The Future of Growth Ep2 to 8.2 times its organic engagement and Will McIntosh's Moment Maker to 7.7 times. Across all 38 September posts the lift was only 1.28 times, because most posts had no such repost. The most-commented posts were people, not announcements: Sara Fischer's honoree poster (60 comments) and Lori Goode's masterclass (37). (C; E; F)

title: Instagram held in September, then faded.
text: Views were 61,587 for Sep 1–28, up 8.5% on August. By Oct 4, 28-day reach was 28,800, down 33% on the 28 days before and a quarter of July's peak. Likes on posts published in the last 30 days fell from 1,230 to 459 on about the same number of posts (38 against 37). September's three best posts were accepted collabs. (Now; A; E)

title: Follower growth is slowing, and a second page splits it.
text: LinkedIn added 3.8% in September against 6.2% a month over the summer, and Instagram is flat at about 8,280. Among peers, ATM ranks sixth on new LinkedIn followers (224 in 30 days), while the duplicate "At The Moment" page added 83 more. Together that would be 307, third among peers. (Now; A; 03)

title: YouTube is organic now, and converts better.
text: With the paid flight over, September views fell to 4,421, 93% below the June–August average that included ads. But September added 50 subscribers, more than the 41 that 180,000 paid views produced across June to August. The channel stands at 111 subscribers. (A; B; 04)

title: The newsletter grew on imports; action did not keep pace.
text: Active subscribers reached 8,407 on Sep 29, up from 5,647 on Sep 1, almost all from imports. Verified human clicks rose to 236 across seven sends, but fell as a share of delivered email, from 0.72% to 0.52%. Site sessions rose 3.4% to 5,739 while users fell 7.2%. (A; 02; 05)

title: Ask every guest and partner to repost with their own words.
text: It is the strongest lever on the page and most posts go without it. Send the guest a ready caption and a link on the day the post goes live.

title: Make Instagram collabs the default.
text: The best posts were collabs and the rest are losing reach. Invite the guest's or brand's account as a collaborator on every post that features them.

title: Lead LinkedIn with named people, not house announcements.
text: People-led posts drew the comments; with reach per post below benchmark, each post has to earn its own audience.

title: Merge the duplicate LinkedIn page.
text: It keeps collecting followers ATM cannot reach. Merged, ATM would move from sixth to third among peers on new followers.

title: Judge YouTube on subscribers and the newsletter on verified clicks.
text: Views fell because the ads stopped and the list grew because of imports; neither number shows whether people are choosing ATM.

title: Followers.
text: LinkedIn's own total was 3,950 on Oct 4. The daily follower chart tracks organic gains from a fixed starting point, so it reads lower (3,631); use it for the trend, not the total.

title: Engagement rate.
text: LinkedIn's own rate counts clicks (about 8.7%). The benchmark row in A leaves clicks out (3.25%) so months compare on the same terms.

title: Time windows.
text: Daily figures run to Oct 4 (LinkedIn reports a day or two late). Monthly figures cover Sep 1–28. Instagram reach and views are Meta's 28-day rolling totals. Engagement momentum counts posts by the date they were published.

title: Subscribers.
text: beehiiv's active count includes imported addresses, so list size alone overstates readers; verified clicks are the better measure.
